 I checked the alleged “fatal issues" carefully, and they are not present in the proof. They appear to come from dropped overlines in automated PDF/math extraction rather than from the actual displayed statements in the paper. Even when the PDF file itself is uploaded, the parsing layer can still lose accents such as $\overline{G_{\mathrm b}}$. In the future, I would strongly recommend checking the displayed PDF visually, or preferably the TeX source from arXiv, for these statements.
I of course welcome careful scrutiny of the proof, but these particular objections are not issues in the paper as written.

A full proof 
claimed by Eric Li (using GPT-5.5 Pro).
 Summary:
 We resolve Erdős Problem #550, originally asked as question of Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp. Precisely, for fixed $k\ge2$ and $1\le m_1\le\cdots\le m_k$, we prove that, for every sufficiently large $n$ and every $n$-vertex tree $T$,\[
 R\!\left(T,K_{m_1,\ldots,m_k}\right)
 \le (k-1)\bigl(R(T,K_{m_1,m_2})-1\bigr)+m_1.
\]The proof combines a new off-Turan tree-embedding theorem with a compactness-and-rounding theorem for represented bounded-rank hypergraph obstructions. The embedding theorem follows from Szemeredi regularity and a local regular-matching embedding lemma of Hladky and Piguet. The compactness argument uses shadow hypergraphs to retain obstructions whose vertices escape along the limiting sequence.
